intent: Using two 100% stacked bars, show that in 1963 Southern states far fewer Nonwhite adults than White adults were registered to vote, and that most Nonwhite adults could not vote.

requirements.question: How large was the 1963 voter-registration gap?
Are all data marks declared by G0 present in the required state or states?

units.claim: In two 100% stacked bars, White registration was 74% versus 40% for Nonwhite adults; 26% of White adults and 60% of Nonwhite adults could not vote.
accept: both White and Nonwhite 100% stacked bars are present
White could not vote = 26% and Nonwhite could not vote = 60%
reject: omitting either registered or could-not-vote segment
showing Nonwhite registration above White registration
units.evidence: Use the corresponding visible bars/segments in the selected keyframe.

units.claim: All 4 required bar marks or stacked segments appear in the final chart.
accept: all 4 required data marks are visible
every grouped bar and every stacked segment is present
the complete required mark set is present in the final chart
reject: omitting any required bar or stacked segment
replacing missing marks with a summary total or subtitle
units.evidence: G0 data-row coverage is rendered as a complete set of identifiable bar marks.
